subject: Service guarantee redlines — uptime, credits, and on-call routing
messages:
From: PilotPay Legal <legal@pilotpay.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Erickson <terickson@pilotpay.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Feb 2028 18:03:00 -0500
Subject: Proposed redlines to Order Form & MSA — uptime / credits / maintenance

Hi Vanessa,

Attached are PilotPay's proposed redlines to the Order Form and limited comments on the MSA focused on the service guarantees. High level items we want to flag up front:

- Uptime target: request for 99.95% monthly availability for the Dedicated tier (we noted Redwood's baseline at 99.9% in the draft).
- Service credits: formula we propose caps at 25% of monthly fees for recurring failures and want a fixed accelerated credit path if availability falls below 99.5%.
- Maintenance windows: PilotPay requests no more than two scheduled maintenance windows per month impacting production, with 72 hours advanced notice and a 4-hour max per window where possible.
- Response / escalation SLAs: For Sev1 incidents we want a 30-minute initial response and 2-hour on-call engagement; for Sev2 a 2-hour response.

We included a PDF with in-text redlines (PilotPay_Redlines_OrderForm_20280212.pdf). Please confirm whether Redwood can accept the maintenance window cap or if you want to propose an alternative. Also flag whether the credits formula needs to be codified differently to align with existing order form fields.

Would appreciate a short timeline for your internal review; PilotPay's procurement counsel hopes to get a signed order form within the next 3 weeks.

Thanks—
PilotPay Legal Team
legal@pilotpay.com

Attachments: PilotPay_Redlines_OrderForm_20280212.pdf
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: PilotPay Legal <legal@pilotpay.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed redlines to Order Form & MSA — uptime / credits / maintenance

Hi PilotPay Legal / Tom,

Thanks for the redlines and the clear summary. We received the PDF and will run a focused review across Legal + Ops. Initial thoughts:

- Uptime: 99.95% is feasible for Dedicated in many regions but has non-trivial cost implications. We should outline the delta in expected monthly fees if we move from 99.9% to 99.95%.
- Maintenance windows: Redwood's standard hosted maintenance practice is weekly short windows; for Dedicated we can offer scheduled windows but need to align on the notice period and maximum per-window duration.
- Credits: we can agree to a tiered credit approach, but want to limit the aggregate cap to a single-month fee or an agreed multiple — we prefer a predictable cap rather than open-ended liability.

Kimberly and Jonas, can you take the ops/feasibility pass and prepare a counterproposal spreadsheet with cost delta and proposed operational language? Laura, please take point on drafting Redwood's tracked redline for the Order Form so PilotPay has a clean comparison.

PilotPay, can you confirm the internal stakeholders who need to approve the cost delta so we can plan the rollout?

I'll follow up by EOD Wednesday with an internal timeline.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 11:07:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Proposed redlines to Order Form & MSA — uptime / credits / maintenance

Vanessa / team,

Quick ops notes after a 30-min sync with infra and capacity planning:

- Cost delta: Moving Dedicated from 99.9% to 99.95% typically requires reserving a larger buffer (additional 10–20% reserved GPU capacity for headroom and preempt mitigation) — ballpark estimate +18% on monthly committed fees for the Dedicated pool in us-west. I'll put exact numbers in the spreadsheet.
- Maintenance windows: We can offer a compromise: 2 scheduled maintenance windows *per calendar month* with a maximum of 3 hours each, and a 72-hour public notice for non-emergency changes. For emergency maintenance (security patches), we need to retain the ability to perform immediate fixes with post-notice reporting.
- On-call/response: We can commit to a 30-min acknowledge for Sev1 and a 2-hour engage for Sev2 during business hours; 24/7 coverage is doable for an additional support add-on.
- Credits cap: ops prefers a single-month bill cap for the aggregate credits; legal may want a multiple-month cap during early contract negotiation.

I'll attach a spreadsheet with the cost delta and proposed language.

Attachments: Redwood_SLA_counterproposal_v1.xlsx

-Kim
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: PilotPay Legal <legal@pilotpay.com>, Tom Erickson <terickson@pilotpay.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 08:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed redlines to Order Form & MSA — uptime / credits / maintenance

Hi Tom / PilotPay Legal —

Thank you for the quick turnaround. Attached is our counterproposal spreadsheet and the suggested tracked changes for the Order Form fields; Laura has started a tracked-redline doc and will circulate a link in the next message. Summary of Redwood's counterproposal:

- Availability: Offer 99.93% for the first 12 months of the Dedicated commitment, with an option to re-evaluate at renewal (we can discuss 99.95% at a higher commit level).
- Maintenance: Two scheduled windows per calendar month, up to 3 hours each, with 72 hours notice; emergency patches excepted with post-event reporting.
- Credits: Tiered credit up to a monthly cap equal to 100% of one month's committed fee; accelerated credits if availability <99.5% as an extra bucket (not cumulative).
- Response: Sev1 30-min ack / 2-hour engage 24x7 as add-on; default included support is business-hours acknowledgement within 30 minutes.

Next steps:
1) Laura will post the tracked-redline link for both Order Form and the MSA excerpt.
2) PilotPay to confirm whether the availability figures are acceptable or whether you want to propose a different economics path (e.g., higher commit for 99.95%).
3) If terms are close, Legal can exchange a clean redline and we can move to DocuSign for the Order Form.

Available for a 30-min call tomorrow afternoon if that helps.

Best,
Vanessa
From: Tom Erickson <terickson@pilotpay.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: PilotPay Legal <legal@pilotpay.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Service guarantee redlines — uptime, credits, and on-call routing

Vanessa / Kim / Laura,

Appreciate the thoughtful counterproposal and the spreadsheet — that helps. A few items from my side:

- 99.93% is a reasonable place to start for the first year. Procurement will want to see the actual delta number (the +18% Kim referenced) so we can budget — can you confirm the modeled monthly delta for a $40k/month committed pool?
- Maintenance: PilotPay can accept 2x/month at 3 hours with 72 hours notice, provided emergency maintenance is limited to high-severity security events and that Redwood documents the post-event communication cadence.
- Credits: We are aligned with a single-month cap for routine issues, but will reserve the right to re-open discussion if there are repeated outages across multiple months.
- Force majeure / SLA exception language: our counsel flagged the MSA’s current force majeure wording as very broad; can Redwood provide a narrower exception list or a time-box for prolonged force majeure events to avoid indefinite SLA suspension?

If you can share the concrete delta for the $40k/month example and the tracked redline link, I can route to Procurement and Legal for a final pass. Happy to join a short call Friday if useful.

Thanks,
Tom Erickson
Head of Platform Partnerships, PilotPay Inc.
terickson@pilotpay.com
